q: Analysis of the Meta ads performance for 2026-10-16 to 2026-10-17: which campaigns work, which waste money, and what should I do?

answer:
Verdict: Meta campaigns returned slightly more than they cost but performance is thin and concentrated — across the 13 campaigns with sales the portfolio spent ₹45,914 and generated net sales ₹51,559 (1.12x net-sales per ₹1 spent) with 26 orders (ad spend per order ₹1,766). This is a small positive return but depends on a few campaigns and many campaigns spent with no sales.

What is working
- Portfolio-level: the 13 campaigns that recorded sales produced net sales ₹51,559 on ₹45,914 spend (orders by order date, 2026-10-16..2026-10-17) → 1.12x net-sales ÷ ad spend.  
- Early signals (too few orders to scale yet): TH-471-PLAYSCRATCHLOUNGE-13OCT-PMF — net sales ₹7,156 on spend ₹3,783.67 = 1.89x (3 orders); TH-075-NAPDEN-16OCT — net sales ₹5,039 on spend ₹2,754.89 = 1.83x (3 orders); TH-264-STORMBORNHARNESS-16OCT-CS — net sales ₹5,165 on spend ₹3,258.85 = 1.58x (2 orders). These look promising but are small samples.

Where money is leaking
- Across all Meta campaigns returned in the paid_media result (120 campaigns with spend), ₹31,383 was spent on 14 campaigns that recorded no net sales in this period — 23.2% of that Meta spend (period 2026-10-16..2026-10-17, paid_media rows). Top campaigns that spent but bought no sales: TH-448-HANDSFREEDOGBELT-13OCT-CS (₹3,696.27), TH-229-BLUEJAY SNEAKS-15OCT-CS (₹3,314.30), CAT SCRATCHERS-CS-10TH-OCT (₹3,305.25), TH-469-SNUGFITSUSPENDERBOOTS-13OCT (₹2,681.26), TH-445-PROSUSPENDERBOOTS-16OCT-CS (₹2,391.79).

Why (what the data supports)
- Performance is concentrated: three campaigns account for ~34.0% of spend.  
- A material share of spend (₹31,383 / 23.2% of Meta spend) bought no measured net sales in the window — this is the clearest source of waste.  
- Several promising campaigns have too few orders to be confident; the data supports testing scale but not wide reallocation yet.

What I would do (ordered by money at stake)
1. Pause / reassign the obvious no-sale spend (quick wins): temporarily stop or reallocate the top campaigns that spent but generated no net sales (top 5 listed above; combined ₹6,620.01 of those five) and re-evaluate after 48 hours; if they still show no orders, keep paused. Check the full list of the 14 no-sales campaigns for smaller quick wins too.  
2. Trim or fix campaigns losing money: reduce budget on high-spend campaigns with net sales < ad spend (example TH-290: spend ₹5,659.14 vs net sales ₹4,640.01) while you investigate landing pages, tracking and audience. If fixes restore conversions, consider cautious reallocation.  
3. Scale small winners carefully: increase budget gradually on the early-signal campaigns (TH-471, TH-075, TH-264 — combined ₹9,797.41) but cap increases (e.g., +25–50%) and monitor orders over the next 3 days; require at least consistent conversion before larger scale.  
4. Investigate targeting/creative and attribution gaps for mid-spend, low-conversion campaigns (CTR/clicks are present on many of them) rather than immediate cut — a technical or landing-page issue can look like wasted spend.

Notes
- Basis: Meta ad spend (paid_media) and net sales on order date (commerce), period 2026-10-16..2026-10-17. Portfolio summary (₹45,914 spend / ₹51,559 net sales / 26 orders) comes from the audit_entities analysis over the 13 campaigns that recorded sales; the no-sales figure (₹31,383 across 14 campaigns) is computed from the full paid_media campaign list (120 campaigns with spend) returned for the same period.  
- Data as of 2026-10-19; platform ad rows are native-time and commerce is order-date. Partial-day caveats do not apply (the period is complete days).
